Chapter One: The Introduction on the Questions of the Akaniṣṭha Deva.
The First Compendium of All Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa Dharmas. Thus have I heard.
At one time the Buddha, the Bhagavān, was dwelling in the celestial realm of Kaṇiṣṭha.
There were countless hosts of devas,
including Kaṇiṣṭha and his retinue.
There were hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of countless hosts of devas;
furthermore, there were hundreds of thousands of millions of bodhisattvas;
and furthermore, there were hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of hosts of devas who preside over giving.
All the great yakṣa generals of the vajras,
together with their retinues,
each sat before the Buddha.
The World-Honored One was surrounded by all the devas and humans.
At that time, the Tathāgata sat upon a lotus flower made of the seven precious substances within a palace made of the seven precious substances;
the palace had four gates opened.
The four pillars were all adorned with the seven treasures;
the palace was lofty and vast,
emitting a great radiance.
Hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of rays of light illuminate the ten directions.
That palace is adorned with canopies made of nets of the seven treasures, which cover it above.
From the four sides of the palace hang various flowered banners, as well as bells and chimes, and standards and pennants made of the seven treasures.
Before that palace were various kinds of flowers and medicinal herbs;
from the body of the Tathāgata, a great radiance was emitted,
manifesting in various mixed colors.
Upon the crown of the Tathāgata’s head,
fully endowed with the thirty-two marks,
he further emitted rays of light of various colors.
That radiance was able to illuminate the trichiliocosm,
reaching upward to the Peak of Existence and downward to the eighteen hells.
That light transformed into clouds of various colored jewels.
From those clouds in the sky, there rained down various kinds of the seven treasures and exquisite lotus flowers of diverse colors,
which spread across the ground;
as well as garments of every sort and ornaments for adorning the bodies of the devas.
From the left side of the Tathāgata’s crown, light radiates forth,
illuminating the Buddhas of hundreds of thousands of billions of worlds throughout the ten directions— [Buddhas adorned with] crowns of the seven jewels, hairpins, earrings, bracelets, and armlets.
The light from the Buddha’s right side shone upon all the Buddhas of the hundreds of thousands of myriads of kotis of immeasurable worlds in the ten directions,
causing them all to leap for joy and rejoice.
All came to rejoice.
From the light on the Tathāgata’s right side,
it pervaded all the devas, nāgas, and yakṣas throughout the world.
Gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, and kiṃnaras.
Mahoragas, humans and non-humans,
and all those born in the hells, asuras, hungry ghosts, spirits, and the human realm.
It illuminates all their karmic offenses and the like;
those sentient beings touched by this light, upon encountering it,
shall all be liberated from every suffering, calamity, and heavy retribution.
It was a marvel, unprecedented and inconceivable.
By the power of that radiance, the gods of Tuṣita Heaven were transformed and reborn in the Heaven of Delighting in Transformations (Nirmāṇarati),
while the other gods each ascended one step higher.
All the devas likewise experienced an increase in their power of merit.
Furthermore, when the Great General Vajrayakṣa saw this,
he was struck with a sense of wonder.
Having attained such inconceivable, marvelous, and wondrous signs of spiritual efficacy as he had never before heard or seen,
he proceeded to the place where the Buddha was,
circumambulated the Buddha three times, and stood before him.
With palms joined in reverence, he prostrated himself;
then, sitting to one side,
he knelt on his right knee and addressed the Buddha, saying:
The World-Honored One is stainless, undefiled, free from greed, and free from anger;
his countenance is bright and serene as he sits upon the seat of *samyaksambodhi*.
The Buddha told Vajrapāṇi:
"What is so extraordinary about this light that all devas, humans, asuras, gandharvas, and others prostrate themselves?
They perform this prostration of the *dharmottama-śīrṣa* (Supreme Dharma-Crown) of all Buddhas."
Furthermore, one attains mastery over the radiance of the body and the body of Samyaksaṃbodhi.
The Tathāgata addressed Vajra, saying:
Excellent, excellent, Vajra!
You are able to bring peace and happiness to all sentient beings;
for the hosts of devas and humans, you are one who can provide liberation through the Dharma.
They create the causes and conditions for others to attain liberation,
so that all may realize the path of *samyak-saṃbodhi* and practice great compassion.
They are able to cause all worlds to obtain this Dharma,
like the utpala flower;
they teach the Vinaya to all sentient beings.
He immediately attained the path of *samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Having heard this Dharma, Vajra praised it, saying:
"Excellent, excellent! It is inconceivable!"
Again, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"How should it be received and upheld?
What is the ritual procedure?"

"I possess the Great Maṇḍala of the Vairocana-garbha, the King of Great Mantra-Seals and Esoteric Arts of the Secret Heart of All Tathāgatas, the Fearless Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa-Hṛdaya Dharma, the Radiant Mass of Great Light, and the various manifestations of the King of Dharma of Various Secret Heart-Mantras."
All have attained inconceivable and sovereign miraculous transformations.
At the time of such transformations,
throughout the Buddha-lands of the three thousandfold world-systems in the ten directions, [all things appear].
It universally illumines all the asuras and other beings throughout the trichiliocosm of the ten directions, including those in the heavens,
the human realm, the hells, the realm of hungry ghosts, and the animal realm.
Those who encounter this light will have all their karmic defilements and afflictions completely extinguished.
This light is of various colors.
There are lights of blue, yellow, red, white, crimson, purple, crystal, and agate.
These lights can rain down flowers of various colors made of the seven precious gems.
This is the ritual of the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa and its maṇḍala rites.
There were such immeasurable numinous wonders.

When the gods of the Kaṇiṣka palace and others heard this teaching of the Great King of Mantras and Seals of the Heart of the All-Tathāgatas, the Vast Accumulation of Jewels,
the Sovereign Crown of the Spiritually Miraculous and Fearless Jewel Buddha, they were moved by it.
Immediately, one attains the Lotus Stainless Samādhi and the Samādhi of Vairocana’s Radiant Appearance;
immediately, one attains the Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa Lotus Fearless Stainless Dhāraṇī Banner.
Immediately, his body and mind became immovable;
he leaped for joy with great delight,
cherishing this Dharma and loving its great bliss.
Furthermore, there was a great general of the Vajra Yakṣas who attained the manifestation of the Vairocana Radiance;
he immediately obtained the Lotus Unstained Dhāraṇī Banner of the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa.
Furthermore, the Great General Vajrayakṣa leaped for joy with a heart and body full of delight,
uttering a profound and most profound lion’s roar of fearlessness in eight kinds of gentle tones.
At that time, Vajrapāṇi took hold of a vajra in his hand,
manifested great majestic power,
and went to where the Tathāgata was.
He circumambulated the Buddha three times,
leaping for joy with great delight,
and having prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, [he departed].
He sat to one side and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, it is as difficult to encounter as the udumbara flower."
